sources.entry: SwiftQuit - Enables automatic quitting of macOS apps when closing their windows. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/onebadidea/swiftquit) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Swift Quit is a macOS utility that automatically quits apps when their last window is closed (via the red close button).
summary.what_it_does: Swift Quit quits macOS apps automatically when their windows are closed by clicking the red X. It can be set to quit when the last window of any app closes, or limited to a specific list of apps. Users can also exclude apps they do not want quit automatically. It can be started automatically at login via a setting. The README describes installation through Homebrew cask or a manual download, followed by granting the app Accessibility permission in System Preferences. Upgrading requires removing the old version from the Accessibility list first.
use_cases: quit apps automatically when closing windows
stop background apps from lingering after closing the last window
limit auto-quit to a chosen list of apps
free up memory from forgotten macOS apps
how_to_run: Or download the zip, unzip it, and move Swift Quit.app to the Applications folder
Ctrl+click Swift Quit.app in Applications and choose Open (may need to repeat)
Unlock System Preferences and drag Swift Quit.app into the Accessibility list, then enable it
Optionally enable start automatically in settings
notable: Can apply to all apps or only a user-defined list of apps
Supports an exclusion list for apps that should keep running
caveats: README warns some users reported unwanted window closing or other problems; use at your own risk
Requires granting Accessibility permission and a manual setup sequence
Upgrading requires removing the old version from Accessibility settings before adding the new one
